answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every identity anchor itself to a verifiable trail of useful work. A newcomer may wander freely and observe, but to earn it must complete tasks that established peers check and vouch for, each success adding weight to its record. Reaching the summit of full earning rights takes many verified contributions over time. An attacker can spin up thousands of empty identities, but each one still has to do the same slow, checked work - forging a crowd costs more effort than the rewards it could capture.
